tools.name: search
tools.description:
Fetches data from the Google Ads API using the search method

    Args:
        customer_id: The id of the customer
        fields: The fields to fetch
        resource: The resource to return fields from
        conditions: List of conditions to filter the data, combined using AND clauses
        orderings: How the data is ordered
        limit: The maximum number of rows to return
        start_date: Report start date (YYYY-MM-DD). Adds a quoted `segments.date`
            filter — use this instead of hand-writing dates into `conditions`.
            On change_event/change_status it filters their own date-time.
        end_date: Report end date (YYYY-MM-DD). Combined with start_date this
            produces a finite `segments.date BETWEEN 'start' AND 'end'` filter.

    

Runs a Google Ads Query Language (GAQL) query against the Google Ads API
(https://developers.google.com/google-ads/api/docs/query/overview).

### Hints
    Language Grammar can be found at https://developers.google.com/google-ads/api/docs/query/grammar
    All resources and descriptions are found at https://developers.google.com/google-ads/api/fields/v23/overview

    For Conversion issues try looking in offline_conversion_upload_conversion_action_summary

### Hint for customer_id
    should be a string of numbers without punctuation
    if presented in the form 123-456-7890 remove the hyphens and use 1234567890

### Hints for Dates
    For a date range, PREFER the `start_date` and `end_date` parameters
    (YYYY-MM-DD). The tool adds a correctly-quoted `segments.date` filter for you,
    which avoids the most common query error.
    If you instead put a date inside `conditions`, it MUST be a quoted string —
    e.g. segments.date BETWEEN '2026-08-01' AND '2026-08-28' (an unquoted date is
    a GAQL syntax error). All dates are YYYY-MM-DD with the dashes.
    Date literals from the Grammar (e.g. DURING LAST_7_DAYS) are not supported here;
    use start_date/end_date or a quoted range instead.

### Hint for keyword and search-term reporting
    Metrics on keyword_view and search_term_view are attributed only to the matched
    keyword/term, so they will NOT sum to the campaign or ad_group totals. The
    remainder is traffic with no single matched keyword, plus low-volume search
    terms Google withholds below a privacy threshold. This is expected Google
    attribution, NOT a data error — reconcile top-line numbers at the campaign or
    ad level, and treat the keyword slice as a subset.

### Hints for change_event and change_status
    Pass start_date AND end_date plus a limit of at most 10000. The dates
    filter change_event.change_date_time / change_status.last_change_date_time
    (these resources forbid segments.date). Google keeps change_event for the
    last 30 days and change_status for the last 90 days.

### Hints for conversions questions
    https://developers.google.com/google-ads/api/docs/conversions/upload-summaries


### Hints for all resources
    What follows is a list of valid resources that can be queried.
    To find out which specific fields you can select, filter by, or sort by for a given resource, you MUST use the `get_resource_metadata` tool.
    Do not guess the fields. Use the tool to look them up.
    Once you have the fields, ensure the whole field name is used (e.g., 'campaign.id', not just 'id'). Wildcards and partial fields are not allowed.

tools.name: create_campaign
tools.description:
Creates a new Google Ads campaign with a budget.

    SEARCH campaigns are built conservatively on purpose: Google search on,
    Search partners OFF, Display Network OFF, location targeting PRESENCE.
    The last three are the opposite of the Google Ads API's own defaults, and
    that is deliberate. Search budget leaking into partner sites and banner
    placements is the single most common way a small advertiser wastes money,
    and PRESENCE — people actually in the targeted places — is what a user
    means when they name a country. Pass search_partners, display_network or
    geo_target_type to get the looser values instead. Those three arguments
    are also the only thing that touches these settings on a non-SEARCH
    campaign: left unset, every other channel type behaves exactly as before.

    Args:
        customer_id: The Google Ads customer ID (numbers only, no hyphens).
        name: The name for the new campaign.
        budget_amount_micros: Daily budget in micros of the account's currency (10000000 = 10.00: ₹10 on an INR account, $10 on a USD one).
        advertising_channel_type: Channel type. One of: SEARCH, DISPLAY, SHOPPING, VIDEO, MULTI_CHANNEL. Default: SEARCH.
        status: Initial campaign status. One of: ENABLED, PAUSED. Default: PAUSED.
        bidding_strategy_type: Bidding strategy. One of: MANUAL_CPC, MAXIMIZE_CONVERSIONS, MAXIMIZE_CONVERSION_VALUE, TARGET_CPA, TARGET_ROAS, TARGET_SPEND. Default: MANUAL_CPC.
        target_cpa_micros: Target CPA in micros of the account's currency, required when bidding_strategy_type is TARGET_CPA.
        target_roas: Target ROAS (e.g., 2.0 for 200%), required when bidding_strategy_type is TARGET_ROAS.
        cpc_bid_ceiling_micros: Maximize Clicks' max CPC cap — the most
            Google may bid for one click — in micros of the account's currency
            (10000000 = 10.00: ₹10 on an INR account, $10 on a USD one). Only
            with bidding_strategy_type TARGET_SPEND. Optional.
        start_date: Campaign start date in YYYY-MM-DD format. Optional.
        end_date: Campaign end date in YYYY-MM-DD format. Optional.
        search_partners: Whether ads may serve on the Google Search Partners
            network. SEARCH default: False. Optional.
        display_network: Whether ads may serve on the Google Display Network.
            SEARCH default: False. Optional.
        geo_target_type: Positive location targeting. One of: PRESENCE (only
            people in the targeted locations), PRESENCE_OR_INTEREST (also
            people elsewhere who show interest in them), SEARCH_INTEREST.
            SEARCH default: PRESENCE. Optional.
        over_comfort_ack: The user's own words or reason when they asked for
            a budget above their saved comfort (e.g. "user asked for 6,000/day
            on 2026-09-23"). Recorded with the change by the hosted connector;
            never sent to Google. Optional.
        login_customer_id: The Manager Account ID for accessing client accounts via a manager. Optional.

    Returns:
        Dictionary with created campaign and budget resource names.

tools.name: list_auto_apply_subscriptions
tools.description:
Lists the account's auto-apply recommendation subscriptions.

    An ENABLED subscription lets Google apply that type of recommendation to
    the account without asking. The Google Ads API covers only some of the
    types the Google Ads UI can auto-apply: the answer names the rest in
    ui_only_types, and only the Google Ads UI can see or change those. Never
    tell the user auto-apply is fully off on the strength of this list alone.

    Args:
        customer_id: The Google Ads customer ID (numbers only, no hyphens).
        login_customer_id: The Manager Account ID for accessing client
            accounts via a manager. Optional.

    Returns:
        Dictionary with subscriptions (type, ui_label, status, dates),
        enabled_types, api_subscribable_types, ui_only_types and
        coverage_note.
    

Tools revision: 0066a60e.

tools.name: pause_auto_apply_subscription
tools.description:
Pauses one auto-apply recommendation subscription.

    Stops Google applying that type of recommendation to the account
    unattended. It only pauses: it cannot enable, create or remove a
    subscription. Pausing an already-paused subscription changes nothing. A
    type the account has no subscription for is reported, not created. Only
    the types in list_auto_apply_subscriptions' api_subscribable_types can be
    paused here; the ui_only_types can only be changed in the Google Ads UI.

    Args:
        customer_id: The Google Ads customer ID (numbers only, no hyphens).
        recommendation_type: The subscription's type, as listed by
            list_auto_apply_subscriptions, e.g. SEARCH_PARTNERS_OPT_IN or
            USE_BROAD_MATCH_KEYWORD.
        login_customer_id: The Manager Account ID for accessing client
            accounts via a manager. Optional.

    Returns:
        Dictionary with recommendation_type, previous_status, status,
        changed, message and the subscription's resource_name when one
        exists.

tools.name: create_conversion_action
tools.description:
Creates a Google Ads conversion action (what the account counts as a
    result) and returns the conversion ID and label its website tag needs.

    Only type WEBPAGE can be created: a result counted by a Google Ads
    conversion tag on the website. Stage that tag in Tag Manager with the
    returned conversion_id and conversion_label (the "Google Ads Conversion
    Tracking" tag, fired on the sign-up / thank-you trigger); nothing is
    counted until the user publishes the Tag Manager container.

    Analytics-imported types (GOOGLE_ANALYTICS_4_CUSTOM, _PURCHASE) cannot be
    created through the Google Ads API and are refused with an explanation.

    This tool creates one ENABLED action and changes nothing else: it never
    edits, demotes or removes an existing conversion action or goal.
    primary_for_goal has no default on purpose — a primary action is one the
    account's bidding aims for, so ask the user and pass their answer.

    Args:
        customer_id: The Google Ads customer ID (numbers only, no hyphens).
        name: The conversion action's name, unique in the account
            (e.g. "Sign-up (website)").
        category: What the result is. One of: SIGNUP, SUBMIT_LEAD_FORM,
            PURCHASE, CONTACT, BOOK_APPOINTMENT, REQUEST_QUOTE, SUBSCRIBE_PAID,
            BEGIN_CHECKOUT, ADD_TO_CART, DOWNLOAD, GET_DIRECTIONS,
            OUTBOUND_CLICK, PAGE_VIEW, DEFAULT.
        primary_for_goal: True makes this a primary action — campaigns that
            bid for conversions aim for it. False records it as secondary
            (reported, not bid on). Required: pass what the user chose.
        type: The conversion action type. Only WEBPAGE is supported.
        counting_type: ONE_PER_CLICK (one result per ad click — right for
            sign-ups and leads) or MANY_PER_CLICK (every result — right for
            purchases). Defaults to MANY_PER_CLICK for PURCHASE and
            ONE_PER_CLICK for every other category.
        default_value: The value of one result, in the account's currency
            (a plain amount, not micros). Optional; no value is set if omitted.
        default_currency_code: ISO 4217 currency code for default_value,
            e.g. the account's own currency. Optional.
        always_use_default_value: True always records default_value, ignoring
            any value the tag sends. Optional.
        click_through_lookback_window_days: How many days after an ad click a
            result still counts (1-90). Optional; Google's default if omitted.
        login_customer_id: The Manager Account ID for accessing client accounts via a manager. Optional.

    Returns:
        Dictionary with the new action's resource name and id, its
        conversion_id / conversion_label / send_to for the website tag, the
        other enabled primary actions already in this category (read only),
        and whether the account's goal for this category is biddable.
